We've made it to Closed Beta! As we continue to chisel away at our feature and bug lists, we're excited to finally be able to get the game into the hands of our backers and early fans of the game.

One of the greatest challenges of game development is making sure you have all fronts covered including marketing, community, quality assurance, business, live operations, game design, art, dev, sound, A/V, etc. When you have a small team dedicated to One Tower, some aspects become neglected when you try to keep your head down to work on the game, including communicating with players, so we've been working hard to have a regular Twitch stream and play session with the devs every Wednesday starting 7/27 @ 5pm PDT. You can follow us at http://www.twitch.tv/onetower to get reminded for when we go online.

As we enter Closed Beta, we are very much aware of some major issues with the game where some functionality is incomplete, or lacks polish. Much of this will be addressed over the coming weeks with regular builds. What we need the most help with from our players is to have the following:

  1. Information on any crashes or major bugs experienced during the game.
  2. Any 'confusion' or pain points that cause frustrations.
  3. Feedback on the game - is it fun? What would make it more fun? What's missing?

You can email your feedback to onetower-feedback@skyreacher.com, or you can respond here on Voat. When possible, please include your player name in any correspondences so that we can look up your account.

Which political ideology do you believe is more efficient towards a prosperous society: social democracy or right-wing libertarianism?

Note: Social Democracy is not Democratic Socialism

Yes it is.

In a society where all information is neutral, democracy equals socialism.

In a right wing libertarian society there is a hierarchy, and most information received by the public comes from the top of that hierarchy. Hence, democracy equals a right wing libertarian society.

Social Democracy is a hybrid economy amalgamating Social safety nets and taxation, while maintaining free market enterprise.

Democratic Socialism was formulated as a transition state from free-market capitalism, engaging temporarily in a hybrid free-market/socialist system, until a transition towards full on Socialism can be made. In my view, Democratic Socialism in the end is pretty much a pre-Socialist state, whereas Social Democracy seems to be compromising between the left and right on economics.

In any case, I myself do find great qualities in both ideologies in regards to their respective visions for prosperity.

Though I do believe greater liberty is attained via right-wing libertarianism, I do have my great respect for what social democracy seems to strive for (making sure that everyone can be assisted during moments of financial adversity. (I'm not engaging in a debate. Again, I actually respect both viewpoints on this.)
